title: POC traffic segmentation & tail profiling — Kestrel Insurance scoping
summary: Initial POC scoping to agree success criteria, traffic segmentation, and benchmark plan. Customer has a mixed bursty QPS profile driven by claims intake and chat assist; they want to validate p95/p99 latency and cost delta between hosted and dedicated. Agreed to run a 48h replay plus synthetic spike tests and share dataset snippets and security docs.
action_items: Maya - send preliminary benchmark config (replay + synthetic spike) by 2026-05-03
Ethan - share replay tooling README and example trace format by 2026-05-03
Anika - provide required SOC2/ISO documentation and KMS policy excerpt by 2026-05-05
Paul - export 48h anonymized traffic sample and token distribution CSV by 2026-05-04
Jordan - schedule 2-hour benchmark kickoff for week of 2026-05-11
next_steps: Run 48h replay on Redwood Dedicated staging + hosted baseline (Maya/Ethan)
Synthetic spike test up to 4x observed peak QPS to validate autoscaling and tail behavior (Ethan/Ravi)
Security review completed and signed NDA addendum (Anika)
Benchmarks reported back with p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, tokens/s, and cost per 1M tokens (Maya)
Follow-up call to review results and decide on pilot configuration (week of 2026-05-18)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 56 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Lara Gomez (Kestrel Head of ML), Paul Rivers (Kestrel Platform), Anika Shah (Kestrel Security), Ravi Menon (Kestrel SRE)

Summary auto (auto-gen): discuss workload segmentation: claims intake chat vs policy underwriting batch rules; want to protect PII and keep on-prem for some workloads.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick agenda — goals, traffic shape, success metrics, then benchmark plan. Lara, can you start with a brief on the workloads?
[00:28] Lara: sure um yeah thanks, on our end there are two primary flows. One is claims intake chat, that's the low-latency customer-facing chat assistant. average QPS is around 4 to 6 during daytime but bursts to ~120 for an hour during major incidents. then we have underwriting batch tasks that run continuously — those are higher token outputs but are not latency sensitive.
[00:58] Paul: to add, we run a routing layer that pins sessions sometimes to a node for sticky KV cache, so concurrency per session matters; we see about 1.2k concurrent sessions at peak but only ~350 active inference QPS sustained.
[01:26] Ethan: ok that's useful. when you say bursts to 120 QPS, is that sustained for 60 minutes or shorter spikes?
[01:35] Lara: usually 30-90 minutes, sometimes chimera events and it's more random night/weekend, but yep 30 to 90 mins typical.
[01:44] Maya: good, so we want to capture both steady-state and tail — you'll want a replay and synthetic bursts. let's get specific about tokens: what are your typical input/output token distributions?
[01:58] Ravi: input prompt lengths for chat average 45 tokens, outputs are 220 tokens avg, but underwriting can produce 1k to 3k tokens per job. the mix is like 70% chat small, 30% long-form batch.
[02:16] Anika: and important: any sample traces we share must be PII redacted, and we require KMS integration for keys, we may want on-prem or VPC private deployment for underwriting flows.
[02:31] Maya: understood. for the POC we can run hosted baseline to get quick numbers and then a dedicated pool in a staging VPC for the replay. we support KMS and on-prem connectors — Ethan will follow up on the exact HSM/KMS APIs.
[02:46] Ethan: yeah I'll include the integration notes. also note our runtime has automatic KV cache and prefix caching — if you pin sessions, we can preserve KV cache hits which lowers per-token compute. sometimes our transcription notes say KV cash which is wrong, lol.
[03:04] Paul: hah, yes KV cache, sorry, we're used to hearing cash in some notes.
[03:12] Lara: back to SLAs, our product team is pushing for p95 < 300ms for chat median user experience and p99 < 800ms. we understand large outputs will be higher.
[03:25] Maya: that SLO is doable for shorter outputs on optimized model variants, but with long output tokens and high concurrency that gets trickier. For the POC scope we should define separate success criteria: 1) chat flow p95/p99 thresholds 2) underwriting throughput (jobs per hour) and accuracy delta 3) cost per 1M tokens below your target.
[03:47] Jordan: can you remind us what accuracy delta looks like for different quantization regimes? we previously saw some regressions when moving to 4-bit.
[03:55] Ethan: yeah, quantization can introduce noise. we'll propose a baseline with FP16 or int8-ish model, then a quantized variant for cost testing. we'll include an eval suite from your golden prompts to measure ROUGE/F1 or business metric.
[04:13] Lara: perfect. timeline wise we want results before underwriting release window on 2026-06-10, so ideally benchmarks done by 2026-05-20 and pilot config decided by 2026-05-25.
[04:27] Maya: OK that's tight but workable. recommended plan: week 1 export and redact sample traces + config, week 2 run replay 48h on hosted baseline, week 3 run dedicated staging replay and spike tests, week 4 analyze and present.
[04:40] Paul: that fits our release cadence. question about concurrency modeling: how do you simulate session stickiness?
[04:48] Ethan: our replay tooling supports session affinity: we replay requests with consistent session IDs so KV cache pathologies show up. we'll also run a synthetic test that migrates sessions randomly to simulate failover.
[05:03] Ravi: good, we care about cold-start tail. also please simulate policy changes that increase output token sizes mid-burst.
[05:12] Ethan: noted. we'll add step-up token size events to spike profile.
[05:18] Maya: benchmarks we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, mem/kv cache hit rate, and cost estimate per 1M tokens on both hosted and dedicate price model.
[05:31] Lara: can you include network egress costs in the cost model, we host some integrations in eu-central so cross-region egress matters.
[05:40] Maya: yep we'll include region-aware pricing.
[05:44] Anika: security: we need SAML SSO, role-based access, audit logs, and key rotation policy. also retention — underwriting logs must be retained 7 years on-prem.
[05:56] Jordan: Redwood Console supports token-level tracing and audit logs; retention can be extended with our enterprise package, and you can configure retention for private deployments. we'll pull the doc.
[06:09] Paul: on dedicated sizing — what sort of headroom should we expect? like for a 120QPS burst with 220 token outputs what GPU pool do you recommend?
[06:20] Ethan: rough back-of-envelope: if you use an optimized 13B quantized variant with warm KV cache, you might get ~80-100 completions/sec per A100-class GPU for short outputs. for 120QPS sustained you'd want 2-3 GPUs with autoscale headroom for 4x spikes. for longer outputs and batch jobs numbers shift; we'll run model-specific profiling.
[06:42] Lara: can you capture the model names? we currently evaluate 'Redwood-Align-13B' internally but names morph. we want consistent model versioning in the report.
[06:52] Ethan: yes we'll pin model sha and quantization profile in the benchmark report. expect a VM image and a model artifact id. some of our transcriptions say Redwood Dedicate, but it's Redwood Dedicated, noted.
[07:04] Maya: on acceptance criteria, propose: chat p95 <= 300ms, chat p99 <= 800ms for 95% of replay windows; underwriting throughput within 10% of current CPU-based throughput; cost per 1M tokens <= your target (please provide target). any objections?
[07:19] Lara: that seems good. our finance target is $120 per 1M tokens for the initial pilot.
[07:25] Maya: great, we'll try to factor that in.
[07:28] Paul: data residency: underwriting must run in our VPC in eu-central only. chat can be hosted in multi-region.
[07:36] Anika: also need SOC2 Type II attestation and penetration test report.
[07:42] Maya: we'll attach security pack and provide SOC2 link. Ethan will also send the penetration testing schedule notes.
[07:50] Jordan: quick note — we'll include a sample dashboard template for the benchmarks with the key KPIs.
[07:58] Lara: great. one more thing: how long does the replay take — if we do a 48h replay at full fidelity how long to run?
[08:07] Ethan: depends on parallelism and concurrency target. if we parallelize to match your QPS profile we can complete a wall-clock 48h replay in roughly the same timeline by replaying in real time; for accelerated profiling we can time-compress but that changes cache behavior. we recommend a real-time 48h run for behavioral fidelity plus a compressed stress run for capacity limits.
[08:30] Maya: action items recap in the meeting notes.
[08:34] -- (cross-talk / setup details exchanged) --
[10:00] Paul: small operational question: if we pin sessions, does Redwood Dedicated keep KV cache sticky across autoscale events?
[10:10] Ethan: we have session migration helpers but on autoscale events cold starts do happen; we'll document best practices (graceful draining, cache prewarm).
[10:22] Lara: ok thanks.
[10:26] Anika: security question — if we do private deployment, who manages the KMS keys?
[10:31] Maya: customer-managed KMS is supported; for on-prem you manage keys and we only handle the control-plane metadata, we can provide an HSM integration guide.
[10:44] Ravi: logistics: we'll anonymize sample traces and drop PII before uploading to your secure bucket?
[10:50] Maya: yes please. we'll provide upload instructions and a minimal schema.
[11:00] Ethan: I'll circulate the replay schema (session_id, timestamp, request_text, response_text, tokens_in, tokens_out, event_type) — note: replace PII with token placeholders or hashing.
[11:15] Lara: quick question on metrics: can you report tokenized prompt vs raw char counts?
[11:20] Ethan: yes we include tokenizer counts. sometimes transcriptions write 'tokenizer' as 'tokenizerer' in our rough notes — ignore that.
[11:30] Maya: ok, plan and timeline again: send config + docs by 2026-05-03, receive redacted traces by 2026-05-04, run hosted 48h baseline week of 2026-05-04, run dedicated staging & spikes week of 2026-05-11, present findings week of 2026-05-18.
[11:52] Lara: sounds good. any blockers? Anika: security docs timeline looks ok.
[12:00] Maya: great. last check — any specific KPIs to add?
[12:05] Paul: include GPU mem pressure and token generation throughput, also % of requests hitting cache.
[12:12] Maya: added. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and set the benchmark kickoff.
[12:20] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcription contains small errors typical of automated transcripts (names/ acronyms occasionally garbled). References to pricing are indicative and subject to formal quote.
